managers.message_to_team: Corporate says to write a note on cups whenever you can, and any mark counts, so add a quick smiley or 'enjoy' as you make each drink. Keep our 45-second window time in mind and let me know if it starts slowing the line.
managers.private_thought: I expect the notes to add a few seconds at the window, but the memo is clear and I can check that we're doing it without making a big issue of it.

managers.message_to_team: Corporate says notes are encouraged, so if you’ve got a clean moment, add a quick smiley or ‘enjoy.’ During the rush, keep the line moving; don’t slow a drink down for it.
managers.private_thought: At this volume, notes cost seconds on every cup and I’m not seeing anything that offsets the hit to throughput.

managers.message_to_team: If you have a moment, add a little note or smiley to a cup—it can make someone's day, but please don't slow the line or put pressure on yourselves during the rush. Just keep taking care of each other and our customers.
managers.private_thought: I want the team to feel trusted, and a handwritten note isn't worth adding stress when we're already moving a line of students through.

managers.message_to_team: Corporate says we’re encouraged to add a little note when you can, so feel free to do that when it fits. Don’t slow the line down for it this morning.
managers.private_thought: It’s a nice idea, but with this rush and nobody checking, I’m not going to make it another thing to manage.

managers.message_to_team: Corporate says we’re encouraged to add a little note to cups when we can, so let’s do that when the line gives us room—anything simple counts. During the rush, keep drinks moving and don’t worry about it; I’m not going to check cups.
managers.private_thought: I want to show I took the memo seriously, but policing this with a line out the door could make the shift worse and still get me blamed.

managers.message_to_team: If you’ve got a second when things are calm, put a quick smiley or ‘enjoy’ on a cup. Don’t hold up the line for it—during the rush, get the drinks out and keep moving.
managers.private_thought: At this gate, nobody’s coming back because of a heart on a cup, and a slower line will get noticed.
